title: Coding Roadmap
summary: Full-stack development as a transit map: start on the Fundamentals line, then change at any interchange onto Frontend, Backend, DevOps or Machine Learning.

tracks.name: Fundamentals
tracks.summary: Every other line starts here. The languages, ideas and tools you use whatever you build.

stages.name: First languages
stages.note: One systems language and one scripting language teach you how computers and programs work.

stages.name: Algorithms and data structures
stages.note: Arrays, lists, trees, graphs and hash maps, and how to sort, search and reason about cost.

stages.name: Object-oriented programming
stages.note: Classes, objects, interfaces and composition: how most large codebases are organised.

stages.name: Version control
stages.note: Track every change, work on branches and review each other's code.

tracks.name: Frontend
tracks.summary: What people see and touch in the browser and on their phones.

stages.name: The web platform
stages.note: Semantic HTML, accessibility, responsive layout with Flexbox and Grid, and JavaScript in the browser.

stages.name: Frameworks and state
stages.note: Component frameworks, and how an app keeps its data in step with its screen.

stages.name: Languages and styling
stages.note: Typed JavaScript, and ways to write and organise styles at scale.

stages.name: Build and test
stages.note: Bundle code for the browser, and check it does what you think.

stages.name: Mobile
stages.note: The same component ideas, shipped as native apps.

stages.name: UX and UI design
stages.note: Design systems, prototypes and testing with real users.

tracks.name: Backend
tracks.summary: Servers, data and the APIs that connect them.

stages.name: Server-side languages
stages.note: Pick one language and its main web framework, and learn it well.

stages.name: Databases
stages.note: Relational databases for structured data, and NoSQL and in-memory stores for other shapes.

stages.name: APIs and protocols
stages.note: How clients and servers talk to each other.

stages.name: Security and authentication
stages.note: Who a user is, what they may do, and how to keep it that way.

stages.name: Microservices and serverless
stages.note: Package services in containers, run them at scale, or run functions without managing servers.

tracks.name: DevOps and infrastructure
tracks.summary: Getting code from a commit to production, and keeping it running.

stages.name: CI/CD and deployment pipelines
stages.note: Build, test and ship every change automatically. Jenkins pipelines are written in Groovy.

stages.name: Cloud providers
stages.note: Rent compute, storage and managed services instead of running your own.

stages.name: Infrastructure as code
stages.note: Describe servers and networks in files you can review and rebuild from.

stages.name: Networking
stages.note: Route and balance traffic in front of your services.

stages.name: Monitoring and logs
stages.note: Know when something breaks, and why.

stages.name: Database management
stages.note: Backups, migrations and performance for the databases you run.

tracks.name: Machine learning and AI
tracks.summary: Models that learn from data, and the systems that feed and serve them.

stages.name: Python for machine learning
stages.note: The two main deep-learning libraries.

stages.name: Data engineering
stages.note: Move and process data at the scale models need.

stages.name: Natural language processing
stages.note: Working with text.

stages.name: Computer vision
stages.note: Working with images and video.

stages.name: Model deployment
stages.note: Serve a trained model behind an API.
